Query-Guided Semantic Change Parsing

A text-only LLM parses requests. Specialist vision models predict the change masks.

A reading guide for the SECOND VLM benchmark discussion

Paper title, abstract and publication record
QSCP02

The task and the outputs

Two registered aerial images plus one request produce three maps.

Input or outputMeaning
T1 and T2The same coordinates at earlier and later observations
Query-specific binary maskOnly changed pixels satisfying the requested relation
T1 semantic mapThe earlier land-cover labels inside the predicted mask
T2 semantic mapThe later labels inside the same predicted mask

QSCP does not ask a general image-input VLM to inspect both images. Specialist semantic heads interpret regions without modifying the mask.

QSCP03

Query meanings

Illustrative paraphrases of the paper’s supported intents, not verbatim benchmark records

IntentExample requestSelected change pixels
To classFind areas that became buildingsDestination = building
From classFind areas that stopped being buildingsSource = building
Involved classFind changes involving buildingsSource or destination = building
Exact transitionFind water converted into buildingsSource = water, destination = building
UnsupportedFind changes to oil tanksEmpty output because class is outside ontology

Bare class names default to the involved-class route.

QSCP04

The fixed SECOND vocabulary

Six land-cover classes

  1. Low vegetation
  2. Non-vegetated ground surface
  3. Tree
  4. Water
  5. Building
  6. Playground

4,662 image pairs

Training2,672
Validation296
Test1,694

Each image is 512 × 512 pixels.

Natural wording can vary. Class identity still resolves to this ontology.

Six evaluation suites on SECOND

SuiteImage–query pairsTarget coverage
All-class10,164Six names per image, including 3,870 empty targets
Present-class6,294Nonempty subset of All-class
Synonym18,882Positive targets under alternate class wording
Sentence32,512Positive targets under intent-bearing sentences
Transition17,632Positive source–destination requests
Unknown1,694Empty targets for unsupported requests

Training uses 120 expressions and 34,595 image–query pairs. Suites overlap in images and sometimes targets.

Paper, section III-B
QSCP06

The language model parses the request

qwen-plus receives text, class definitions and intent definitions. It does not inspect the images.

Parsed fieldRole
IntentTo, from, involved, or exact transition
ClassThe queried category for a class request
Source and targetThe ordered category pair for a transition
Support flagWhether the request fits the fixed ontology

Alias normalization maps alternate names to canonical classes. Repeated text responses are cached. Temperature is 0.

Reported exact-route accuracy: 99.94% on 1,549 distinct transition expressions and 100% on the other controlled suites. This measures parsing within the bank.

The complete architecture

Pretrained RCDNet supplies directional evidence. Learned correction and semantic decoding use image features and parsed intent.

Original figure 1 reproduced from Qian and Ma. Follow the paper’s labels for the exact module connections.

QSCP08

A request selects a temporal operation

RouteScore map before thresholdingInterpretation
To class cPctoEvidence entering class c
From class cPcfromEvidence leaving class c
Involving cPcto + PcfromEither temporal direction
Source s to target tPtto × PsfromSpatial agreement of both endpoints
Unsupported0No visual inference can add a new class

RCDNet runs in both image orders. Directional correction fuses with its outputs in log-odds space, using weight 0.25.

Paper, equations 2–6
QSCP09

What training and calibration contribute

Specialist visual prediction

The official pretrained RCDNet checkpoint supplies features and class-conditioned change evidence.

Decoders train in stages. During semantic-head training, RCDNet, CLIP and the direction decoder stay frozen.

Additional semantic supervision

Both temporal labels supervise the query region. Broader directional masks expose alternative origins and destinations.

CLIP ViT-B/32 supplies text features. Seven output labels include background.

Validation locks: whole-image threshold 0.60, class-intent threshold 0.55, transition threshold 0.20. Components smaller than 64 pixels are removed.

QSCP11

Three metrics answer different questions

MetricWhat it measuresReading caution
BIoUMean of pooled changed-pixel and unchanged-pixel IoUIncludes the background class
Sem.GTTemporal foreground semantic mIoU on ground-truth regionsSupplies correct localization
E2E-SemTemporal foreground semantic mIoU including predicted-mask errorsIncludes missed and spurious regions

Transition BIoU is 70.99%. The separately reported positive-mask IoU is 28.03%.

Neither is directly comparable to another evaluator’s macro average over supported transition strata without recomputing predictions.

RCDNet receives raw text. Several other baselines use keyword adapters that return empty masks for unmatched wording.

Large language-suite gains combine parsing and routing with visual prediction. They do not isolate better visual transition recognition.

QSCP13

Semantic maps explain the selected changes

On Present-class, QSCP reports 62.35 Sem.GT and 38.01 E2E-Sem. Localization errors lower the complete-system score.

For exact transitions, the query already supplies both class names. High semantic accuracy inside those regions needs this conditioning stated.

Original figure 3. Black denotes background or regions excluded by the query.

Paper, figure 3 and section III-H
QSCP14

Transfer and two kinds of empty output

WHU-CDC evaluation uses 744 pairs: 181 changed and 563 unchanged. The bank has 19 expressions, with 15 supported variants and four unsupported requests.

Empty-output testQSCP resultMeaning
Unsupported class100% rejectionThe parser rejects a request outside the ontology
Supported building query on absent change16.70% rejectionThe visual system must recognize absence

All 15 supported expressions normalize to one involved-building route. Their identical 70.94 BIoU reflects identical masks for equivalent requests.

No target-domain training or recalibration. WHU’s binary labels do not evaluate directional multiclass transitions.

Paper, sections III-A–B and III-I
QSCP15

What the paper establishes

  • A structured parser can connect varied expressions to a fixed set of temporal operations.
  • Specialist directional predictions can produce a query mask and paired semantic maps.
  • Equivalent wording can yield identical masks through canonical routing.

What remains outside this evidence

  • Arbitrary unseen-class recognition or unrestricted language understanding
  • Frozen general VLMs selecting transitions directly from two images
  • A broad test of within-class physical modification
  • Reliable rejection of every supported-but-absent change
Paper, sections II–III; repository task scope
QSCP16

Comparison with general chat VLM evaluation

Already covered by QSCPGeneral chat VLM evaluation
Source, target, involvement and transition requestsWhether general VLMs apply these relations from visual evidence
Synonyms and sentence queriesPrompt search and held-out transfer without weight updates
Parser plus specialist visual modelFree localization versus supplied-region temporal selection
Background-aware query segmentation scoresExplicit foreground metrics with matched target difficulty

Research interpretation: the query task overlaps. QSCP does not benchmark chat VLMs on image pairs plus questions. A direct ChatGPT / DeepSeek / GLM evaluation addresses a different evaluation setting. Its contribution depends on coverage and evidence.
